title: Copy List With Random Pointer
statement: Every node of a linked list has a value, a next pointer and a random pointer. Random may point at any node in the list, or at null. Build a deep copy: brand new nodes with the same values, where every pointer points inside the new list. No new node may point at an old node.

example.caption: Input and copy look the same. The copy is made of new nodes. Dashed arrows are random pointers.

idea.sentence: Make one new node per old node and keep a map from old to new, then every pointer in the copy is just the map applied to the old pointer.

jargon.plain: A copy that shares no node with the original. Change one list and the other does not move.
An extra pointer on each node that can aim at any node of the same list, before or after it, or at itself.

watch.inputHint: One argument: a list of [value, randomIndex or null] pairs, e.g. [[7,null],[13,0],[11,1]]

compare.bruteLabel: Copy next pointers, then walk the list to find each random target
compare.optimalLabel: Look each target up in a map

rows.name: Find targets by walking
rows.note: For every random pointer, count how far the target is from the head, then walk that far in the copy.

rows.name: Old to new map
rows.note: Three simple passes. Each pointer is one map lookup.

rows.name: Interleave the copies
rows.note: Weave each new node right after its old one, so old.next is the twin. Not shown here. It needs careful unpicking at the end.

fast.takeaway: A map turns 'where is the twin of that node?' into one step. Memory for the map buys the drop from quadratic to linear.

stages.title: One twin per node
stages.note: Walk the list. For each old node make a new node with the same value, and store old -> new in the map. No pointers set yet.

stages.title: Wire next
stages.note: For each old node, the twin's next is the twin of the old next. A null stays null.

stages.title: Wire random
stages.note: Same move: the twin's random is the twin of the old random. The map finds it at once, even if it is far ahead.

stages.title: Return the new head
stages.note: The twin of the old head is the head of the finished copy.

edges.title: Empty list
edges.why: The head is null. Both loops do nothing and the twin of null is null.

edges.title: Random to itself
edges.why: The twin must point at itself, not at the old node. The map gives exactly that.

edges.title: Random points forward
edges.why: A random target can be a node you have not reached yet. Making all twins first means it already exists.

edges.title: Equal values
edges.why: Do not key the map by value. Three nodes holding 3 would collide. Key by the node itself.

gotchas.text: Make every twin before you wire anything. Wiring in the same pass fails when random points at a node that has no twin yet.
The map must be keyed by the node, never by its value. Values repeat. Node identity does not.
Map<Node, Node> compares keys by reference, which is what we want here. map.get(null) is a type error, so wrap it in a small helper that returns null for null.
Reading a missing key gives the zero value, and for a pointer map that is nil. So copies[nil] is nil with no special case, and you can skip the nil checks.
Returning the original head by mistake still looks right when printed. Check that no node is shared.

recap.pattern: Linked list: old to new map
recap.key: First make a twin of every node and remember old -> new. Then set each twin's next and random with one lookup each.
moves: Map old node -> new node for all nodes
